SELECTED_INDEX: 3  
CONFIDENCE: 0.22  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by a very strong band at 671 cm⁻¹ that fits the typical C–S stretching region (≈ 600–720 cm⁻¹). Two medium-intensity bands at 1041 and 1058 cm⁻¹ match the C=S stretching region of thioketones (≈ 1030–1100 cm⁻¹; cf. Nakamoto rule GFQ-052 for C=S ≈ 985–1080 cm⁻¹). Candidate 3 (CCC(O)C=S) is the only molecule that contains both a C–S single bond and a C=S thiocarbonyl group, rationalising these key peaks. The strong C–H stretches at 2913–2984 cm⁻¹ and the CH₃/CH₂ deformation at 1465 cm⁻¹ are fully consistent with its aliphatic framework. The weak bands near 2660–2760 cm⁻¹ can arise from hydrogen-bond–broadened O–H stretching of the alcohol group in this molecule, supporting its presence. Other candidates either lack a C=S group (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10) or would be expected to show distinctive stretches (e.g., N₃ at ~2100 cm⁻¹ for 2, strong C–F near 1000–1100 cm⁻¹ plus no O–H band for 5) that are absent or inconsistent. Hence candidate 3 best fits the observed Raman features.
